paper.title_en: Photoproduction of \(K^{0}\Sigma^{+}\) off protons in the resonance region
paper.abstract_en: We analyze the \(\left. \gamma p\rightarrow K^{0}\Sigma^{+} \right.\) process in the resonance region within the framework of the isobar model. The amplitude is constructed as a sum of tree-level Feynman diagrams with the addition of the contact current ensuring gauge invariance of the total amplitude. The resonance content of our models is inspired by a model for the isospin-related \(K^{+}\Sigma^{0}\) channel. The main coupling constant in the \(K\Sigma N\) vertex is estimated with the help of isospin symmetry, and the rest of the free parameters (resonance couplings and hadronic form-factor cutoffs) are calibrated to the available \(K^{0}\Sigma^{+}\) data. Using the resulting models, we calculate the differential and total cross sections as well as polarization observables \(\left( P \right.\), \(\Sigma\), \(T\), \(O_{x}\), \(\left. O_{z} \right)\), and compare them with measurements. We identify the \(N(1720)3/2^{+}\) and \(N(1900)3/2^{+}\) states as the most important ones for good correspondence with the experimental data.
